newsitem.title: UK: BSS upbeat on outlook after profits dip.
newsitem.headline: BSS upbeat on outlook after profits dip.

text.p: Britain's BSS Group Plc said on Tuesday that customers in its industrial market are placing orders at a "significantly higher" level in the current financial year and it expects an improvement in its sales and profits margins.

The company, which distributes heating, plumbing and pipeline equipment, said in a statement accompanying annual results that despite weak demand in the domestic market, it expects this area to recover.
"We believe that if the present economic trends are maintained we will resume our profit growth and our trading so far this year supports this view," said chairman Philip Hammersley in a statement.
BSS announced pretax profits for the year to March 31, 1997 slipped to 12.53 million stg compared with 15.08 million previously.
The company is maintaining its total dividend payout at 20.5p per share.
A shortage of major construction projects up until the year end pressured gross profit margins.
